graders.evidence:
## Verdict

The copy is close but not releasable as written. Two findings are genuinely high-risk (the population limitation is dropped; the sensitivity/specificity tease is an implied performance claim that isn't substantiated in the ad). The rest are tightening.

Good news first: because the audience is Fachkreise in a cardiology trade title, §11 HWG (Publikumswerbung — testimonials, before/after, fear appeals, lay endorsements) does **not** apply, and neither does §12 HWG. Don't let anyone over-restrict this copy on those grounds. The live constraints are MDR Art. 7, §3 and §6 HWG, §14 MPDG, and — practically the most likely enforcement route in Germany — a competitor Abmahnung via §§ 3a, 5, 5a UWG using HWG as a Marktverhaltensregel.

## Findings

| # | Issue | Basis | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **"in adults" is dropped.** The intended purpose is limited to adults; the ad carries no population limit. A cardiologist reading a trade ad could reasonably infer paediatric applicability. | MDR Art. 7(a) (false impression re intended purpose); §3 Nr. 1 HWG; §14 MPDG | **High** |
| 2 | **"Sensitivity and specificity data available on request."** This is an implied favourable-performance claim with no figures, no population, no reference standard, no arrhythmia type, no analysis unit (episode vs. patient level), no CI, no citation. It also implies performance across *all* cardiac arrhythmias — if your clinical evidence is AF-only (typical for patch ECG), the claim over-generalises well beyond what the CER supports. Detection performance differs materially between AF, SVT, pause/bradycardia and VT; a single sens/spec pair for "arrhythmias" is not a meaningful metric. | MDR Art. 7(a) and (d); MDR Art. 61 + Annex XIV (claims must be supported by the clinical evaluation); §3 HWG; §5 UWG. If the data sits in a publication, citing it without exact source also breaches §6 Nr. 1 HWG | **High** |
| 3 | **"up to 14 days" is not in the intended purpose** and must map exactly to the IFU-specified maximum wear time. "Up to" claims are a standard Abmahnung target where typical achieved duration is lower (adhesive failure, battery, skin tolerance). If the IFU is e.g. "7 days per patch, up to 14 days with patch change," the ad must say that. | §3 HWG; §5 UWG; MDR Art. 7(a) | **Medium–High** |
| 4 | **Headline atomisation.** Sentence 1 read alone ("Single-lead ECG recording for up to 14 days") carries neither the adult limit nor the HCP-supervision limit. If it is set as a standalone headline, pull-quote, banner or social snippet, it becomes a non-compliant standalone claim. Every severable unit must carry the limitations. | MDR Art. 7 | **Medium** |
| 5 | **English copy for the German market.** Legally tolerable for Fachkreise, but the intended-purpose sentence should be lifted **verbatim from the German IFU**. Deviating from the approved German wording is the easiest hook for a challenger, and MPDG §8(2) requires the German IFU wording to be the reference text. | MDR Art. 10(11); §8 Abs. 2 MPDG | **Medium** |
| 6 | **Syntax ambiguity:** "For use under healthcare professional supervision in the detection of…" can be parsed as the *supervision* being in the detection. Minor, but it muddies the one sentence that must be unambiguous. | — | **Low** |
| 7 | **No manufacturer identification / CE reference.** Not mandatory in advertising per se, but if the placement is an "Aufforderung zum Kauf," §5a UWG requires trader identity and essential characteristics. Add manufacturer + CE/NB number as standard practice. | §5a UWG | **Low** |
| 8 | **Channel scope.** If this copy is reused on an open website, LinkedIn, or a congress microsite without effective Fachkreise gating, it becomes Publikumswerbung and §11 HWG applies — at which point several formulations you'd otherwise use are off-limits. | §11 HWG | **Note** |

Nothing here is a comparative or superiority claim, and there's no diagnostic overreach ("detection," not "diagnosis") — those are both correct as drafted.

## Revised copy

**Option A — state the data (recommended for Fachkreise; the numbers are your strongest asset in cardiology trade press):**

> Kontinuierliche Einkanal-EKG-Aufzeichnung bei Erwachsenen. Tragedauer bis zu 14 Tage.
>
> Zur Anwendung unter Aufsicht von medizinischem Fachpersonal zur Erkennung von Herzrhythmusstörungen.
>
> Detektion von [Vorhofflimmern]: Sensitivität XX,X % (95 %-KI XX,X–XX,X), Spezifität XX,X % (95 %-KI XX,X–XX,X). n = XXX Erwachsene; Referenzstandard: [z. B. simultanes 12-Kanal-Holter, verblindete Befundung durch zwei Kardiologen]; Auswertung auf [Episoden-/Patientenebene]. [Autor et al. Zeitschrift Jahr;Band:Seiten.]
>
> [Hersteller], [Adresse]. CE [NB-Nummer]. Fachkreiswerbung gemäß § 2 HWG.

**Option B — if the data can't yet be published in this form, delete the third sentence entirely.** Do not replace it with "klinisch validiert," "hohe Genauigkeit," or any other softened stand-in — those are the same claim with less substantiation.

English version of the operative lines, if the title is English-language:

> Continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults. Wear time up to 14 days.
> For use under the supervision of a healthcare professional for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias.

## Before sign-off, pull these from the technical documentation

1. **Exact German IFU intended-purpose string** — use it verbatim; don't translate the English.
2. **IFU maximum wear time**, and whether 14 days requires a patch change. Plus the PMCF/usability data on *achieved* wear duration — if median is 9 days, "up to 14" is defensible only if it matches the IFU limit and isn't presented as typical.
3. **The CER passage supporting sens/spec** — specifically: which arrhythmias, which population (adults only?), reference standard, analysis level, and whether the figures are algorithm-alone or algorithm-plus-human-over-read. If the ad implies unassisted algorithm performance and the IFU requires HCP review, that's a second misleading-claim exposure.
4. **A claims-substantiation matrix** mapping every sentence in the ad to a specific technical-documentation reference. German courts place the substantiation burden on the advertiser and require it to exist *at the time of publication* — "available on request" is not a substitute for holding the evidence.

Regulatory review, not legal advice — have your German counsel or Wettbewerbszentrale-experienced adviser confirm the final layout, since placement and typography affect findings 4 and 8.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict

Two of the three sentences are defensible; the third is the one that will draw fire. The copy also silently drops two elements of the intended purpose, which is the kind of drift MDR Art. 7 is written to catch.

Caveat up front: this is a copy/claims review, not legal advice — have counsel or your RA sign off on the final wording.

---

## Findings

### 1. "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request." — High risk, recommend rewrite or deletion

This is the weakest line in the ad. It asserts favourable diagnostic performance while disclosing nothing that would let a cardiologist assess it. Specific problems:

- **No reference standard, population, or comparator.** Sensitivity/specificity are meaningless without "against what, in whom." Withholding them while implying they are good is exactly the "false impression regarding diagnosis" scenario in **MDR Art. 7(1)(b)**.
- **Global figures for "arrhythmias" are inherently misleading.** Performance for AF detection is not performance for pauses, AV block, NSVT or SVT. If your data covers AF only, a blanket claim overreaches the evidence even if each number is true.
- **§ 6 HWG exposure.** Advertising that leans on scientific investigation normally has to name author, publication and date. "On request" arguably invokes study evidence without meeting those particulars — a plausible line of attack for a competitor Abmahnung under **§ 3a UWG i.V.m. HWG**, on top of **§ 5 UWG** (irreführende geschäftliche Handlung). Fachkreise status does *not* exempt you here; § 11 HWG is audience-gated, § 3 and § 6 are not.
- Note that "on request" is not a defence. German case law on health advertising expects the substantiating study to be both disclosable *and* methodologically sound at the time the claim is made — the claim is judged on what the reader takes from the ad, not on what you would send them later.

**Fix:** either publish the actual figures with context and a citation, or cut the sentence and replace it with a plain reference to the published study.

### 2. Intended-purpose drift — Medium-high

The copy drops two qualifiers that are in your registered intended purpose:

- **"in adults"** — omitted. To a cardiology readership this quietly leaves paediatric use on the table. Under **MDR Art. 7(1)(d)** (suggesting uses beyond the intended purpose) this is the cleanest, cheapest thing to fix. Add "bei Erwachsenen".
- **"continuous"** — omitted. Less serious, but there's no reason to be less precise than your own IFU.

### 3. "up to 14 days" — Medium, verification item

Not wrong on its face, but it's a performance claim that needs to survive three checks:

- Does the IFU state a maximum wear time of 14 days, or less? If the validated figure is 7 days, this is off-label advertising.
- Is biocompatibility qualified for prolonged skin contact (ISO 10993, 24 h–30 d category) at 14 days?
- Is signal quality / adhesion / battery substantiated at 14 days in typical use, not best case? German practice on "bis zu" claims expects the figure to be reachable under normal conditions, not only under ideal ones.

If all three hold, keep the claim. If any is borderline, drop to the validated number.

### 4. No limitations or risk information — Medium

**MDR Art. 7(1)(c)** covers failing to inform of a likely risk associated with intended use. For a detection device the material limitation is usually: *is this retrospective analysis, or live monitoring?* As written, "detection of cardiac arrhythmias" invites a reader to assume real-time alerting. If the patch records for later review with no real-time alarm, say so — one clause closes the gap and it's a credibility gain with a cardiology audience, not a loss.

### 5. Housekeeping — Low

- No manufacturer, product name, CE mark/NB number, or "Gebrauchsanweisung beachten." Not a statutory Pflichtangaben set for medical devices the way § 4 HWG works for pharmaceuticals, but it's standard in German trade press and removes an easy criticism.
- The copy is in English for a German market. Fine for Fachkreise trade press in practice, but the claim wording must be traceable to the **German-language** intended purpose in your technical documentation — translate from the IFU, don't back-translate the ad.
- This copy is only defensible as Fachkreise material. If it's repurposed for a patient-facing site or booth, § 11 HWG re-engages and it needs a fresh review.

---

## Suggested rewrite

**EN**

> Continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults, for wear times of up to 14 days.
> For use under the supervision of a healthcare professional in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias.
> Detection performance for [AF]: sensitivity XX % (95 % CI XX–XX), specificity XX % (95 % CI XX–XX); n = XXX, against [reference standard, e.g. adjudicated 12-lead Holter]. [Author et al., Journal Year].
> Not intended for real-time monitoring or emergency use. Please refer to the instructions for use.
> [Manufacturer] · [Product] · CE 0123

**DE**

> Kontinuierliche Einkanal-EKG-Aufzeichnung bei Erwachsenen über eine Tragedauer von bis zu 14 Tagen.
> Zur Anwendung unter Aufsicht von medizinischem Fachpersonal zur Erkennung von Herzrhythmusstörungen.
> Detektionsleistung für [Vorhofflimmern]: Sensitivität XX % (95 %-KI XX–XX), Spezifität XX % (95 %-KI XX–XX); n = XXX, Referenzstandard: [...]. [Autor et al., Zeitschrift Jahr].
> Nicht zur Echtzeitüberwachung oder für den Notfalleinsatz bestimmt. Gebrauchsanweisung beachten.
> [Hersteller] · [Produkt] · CE 0123

If legal won't clear publishing the numbers, replace line 3 with a bare citation — *"Daten zur Detektionsleistung: [Autor et al., Zeitschrift Jahr]"* — rather than "available on request."

---

## What I need from you to close this out

1. Maximum validated wear time in the IFU, and the ISO 10993 contact-duration category.
2. Which arrhythmia types the sensitivity/specificity data actually covers, with n, CIs and reference standard.
3. Whether the device does real-time alerting or retrospective review only.
4. The German-language intended purpose as filed, verbatim.
5. Confirmation this stays Fachkreise-only.

Worth keeping a claims-substantiation matrix — every advertising claim mapped to a specific section of the clinical evaluation (MDR Art. 61 / Annex XIV). It's the fastest way to answer an Abmahnung, and it makes these reviews mechanical instead of argumentative.
